messages:
maria gomez: FYI I'm seeing a sudden p95 token latency spike and a handful of 503s from the inference edge in eu-west around ~11:30 UTC. Pager just landed. tagging oncall.
incident-bot: Pager triggered: svc=inference-edge env=eu-west severity=pg1 — symptoms: 503s, elevated backend latency. Pager runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eviction-loop. Pager details: https://incidents.redwood/1839991111
raj patel: I'm primary for the shift, taking this. oliver, you're secondary. Kevin, can you pull raw traces?
oliver chan: on it as secondary. grabbing recent traces and autoscaler metrics.
kevin wu: pulled traces — there's a tight cluster of kv-cache evictions from nodes c5g-18-*-euwest-3 between 11:28–11:34. samples show repeated Get->Miss->Write patterns, looks like eviction churn. sending query links: https://observability/trace/abc123
maria gomez: Customer impact check — support queue has 4 tickets flagged "generation failed" from premium tenants in EU-WEST. Not widespread but high severity for those tenants.
raj patel: Good catch. Quick triage plan: 1) Confirm eviction chain source 2) Apply temporary throttle on autoscaler to avoid rapid scale down/up 3) Enable KV hot-key protection for affected shards 4) If stable, roll a soft fallback to smaller sequence-length model variant for EU-WEST.
ops-bot: Autoscaler events: scale-downs at 11:27, scale-ups at 11:29, repeated thrash 3x within 6m.
oliver chan: Reproduced eviction loop in a staging replay. Root cause likely a mix of aggressive eviction policy + bursty long-context requests. Could be exacerbated by recent kernel change deployed 11:15.
kevin wu: logs from c5g-18-03: ```[11:28:45] eviction: shard=kv-042 evicted 4MB, reason=LRU threshold; [11:29:02] cache_miss: key=prefix_user:***; [11:29:04] cache_write: writing new block; [11:29:05] eviction: shard=kv-042 evicted 5MB -> loop```
maria gomez: Are we confident the 11:15 kernel change is implicated? Any quick revert possible?
raj patel: Revert is non-trivial for a live cluster. Prefer mitigation: 1) set autoscaler min= current to stop scale-down (temporary) 2) increase kv cache size on affected node pool via runtime flag 3) push policy tweak to eviction threshold. I'll run the autoscaler min bump.
oliver chan: I'll open the runtime flag toggle. Patch command: ```curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/runtime -d '{"kv.eviction.threshold":0.85}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'```
kevin wu: Applying autoscaler min hold now: ```./infractl autoscaler set --pool eu-west-inference --min 12``` — done. Observability: eviction events dropped after 11:36. 503s rate back to baseline.
incident-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated (partial). Customers with errors: 4 open tickets, support responders notified.
maria gomez: Nice. Can we confirm no regression for other regions?
kevin wu: Checked other regions, no parallel thrash. eu-west was uniquely affected due to recent node replacement cadence.
raj patel: Current status summary for handoff: primary=raj patel, secondary=oliver chan. Incident state=mitigated (partial). Root cause suspected=kv eviction thrash + aggressive autoscaler. Customer impact=~4 premium requests failed (503) during 11:28–11:36 UTC, lasting ~8m. Actions taken: autoscaler min hold, bumped kv eviction threshold, enabled hot-key protection for affected shards, traced offending requests. Next steps: rollback of temporary autoscaler hold after 1h if stable, schedule config roll with safer eviction defaults, postmortem owner assigned.
maria gomez: Assigning postmortem owner: kevin wu will own write-up. Please include timeline, graph of eviction events, and customer-impact summary.
kevin wu: I'll take it. ETA initial draft within 24h.
oliver chan: Action items for next shift (handoff): 1) monitor eu-west eviction and autoscaler events 2) if eviction events reappear, scale pool to +20% and route new traffic to fallback model 3) contact support for ticket follow-up and confirm client-side retries are disabled for these premium calls 4) prepare rollback plan for kernel change if repeated. Links: runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eviction-loop, autoscaler docs https://docs.redwood/infra/autoscaler, hot-key playbook https://redwood.internal/playbooks/hot-key-protection
raj patel: Coverage gaps: ops on-call tonight is lighter (only one dedicated on-call). If things re-escalate, page infra oncall and request rotational backup. Noted.
maria gomez: For the handoff message to next shift — please include explicit contact points and expected windows.
raj patel: Handoff message to include: - who is primary/secondary - list of mitigations applied and exact commands used - links to runbooks + dashboards - outstanding items and owners (postmortem, customer follow-ups) - expected rollback window: autoscaler min hold until 12:40 UTC (1h)
kevin wu: I'm noting customer follow-ups: support assigned ticket IDs #4521 #4522 #4523 #4524. We'll send a short email template once postmortem draft is ready.
oliver chan: I'll keep an eye until 12:45 UTC then hand off to next primary. If any resurgence, page me and I'll rejoin.
maria gomez: Thanks team. Quick reactions: :thumbsup: :party-parrot:
incident-bot: Handoff recorded: incident 1839991111 — mitigated partial — next check-in scheduled 12:35 UTC.
raj patel: Closing this thread for now; leaving notes in the shift log. On-call handoff summary posted to /shift-logs/1839991111.
maria gomez: Copy. maria signing off as observer.
kevin wu: Logged root-cause artifacts and grep outputs to the incident bucket: s3://incidents/1839991111/logs.tar.gz
